question: Under the original Hangzhou demand, do heavier right/straight merge conditions recur outside the two sampled time windows?
basis: Both pilot seeds supplied a switchable merge, but all 18 Hangzhou observations had exactly one near right-turn vehicle and at most four near straight vehicles. Only one of the eight observed Jinan tradeoffs had a joint supply count seen in this pilot.
design: Use the same admitted aligned source package and PP controller, two new development seeds 32061101 and 32061102, each for 3600 seconds. Measure all 16 signals at every scheduled 10-second epoch, 0 through 3590. Keep eligibility and empty-supply counts by seed. Use the existing movement registry, 10-second near-distance rule and full matched right-signal timeline.
readout: Compare the full joint count distribution with all 15 frozen Jinan observations, including straight supply 8–11 and multiple right-turn vehicles. Report distinct visits to high-supply conditions as well as the duration and per-seed counts so adjacent ticks of one queue are identifiable. Summaries only leave the server.
decision: Stop on collision or teleport. Use whole-seed recurrence and the joint supply distribution to judge whether there is enough common support to design a separate matched response collection. If heavier conditions are absent or confined to one seed, close this unchanged-demand source for the full-target claim. Preserve the low-load result.
